Concise Clinical Note

Consult Summary:
25-year-old woman with 2-day history of constant dull lower-abdominal ache, nausea, and subjective fever/sweats; GP advised urgent face-to-face review and pregnancy test.

History:
• Presenting complaint: Constant dull ache below the umbilicus for 2 days, associated nausea; feels hot and sweaty.  
• No vomiting, no diarrhoea.  
• Genitourinary: Increased urinary frequency without dysuria, urgency, odor, or pain; notes pink tinge in urine over last couple of days and is due for menses (LMP ~3+ weeks ago). Sexually active; contraceptive implant in situ.  
• Bowels: Constipated one week ago, resolved; normal bowel motion yesterday.  
• Pertinent negatives: No light-headedness, no vaginal discharge.  

Past Medical History: None reported.  
Allergies: Amoxicillin – nature of reaction not specified.  
Medications: Etonogestrel implant (Implanon) – dose/route/frequency not documented.  
Social: Non-smoker; lives with boyfriend.  
Family History: Brother with type 1 diabetes.

Examination:
Vitals: not documented.  
Physical findings: not examined (video/telephone consult).

Impression:
Lower-abdominal pain with nausea – differential includes early pregnancy/ectopic, urinary tract pathology, gastrointestinal causes (e.g., constipation). Pregnancy must be ruled out.

Plan:
• Arrange same-day face-to-face GP review for abdominal and pelvic examination.  
• Perform point-of-care or laboratory pregnancy test.  
• Consider urine dipstick, urinalysis, and further investigations as indicated.  
• Safety-netting: If pain or nausea worsens, develops light-headedness, fainting, or other concerning symptoms, seek urgent medical attention.  

Quality checks:
● Missing expected elements: physical examination, vitals, full allergy details, medication list confirmation.  
● No internal transcript conflicts noted.  
● Transcript quality acceptable; minor conversational overlaps but clinically clear.
